comment: After the second paragraph the post loses its thread: it lists options and tools, then jumps straight to "To test how accurate..." and a run of three percentages. Nothing says why the test mattered, so the reader's attention drops. Each paragraph should follow from the one before: why the test was needed, what was tested, what the result means (with the number inside the sentence), and the decision it led to.

Rejected. 1) Media: no graphs at all. The document pages repeat the post's own sentences (question in large type, answer in small type) and the results page is a list of numbers. Every page must be a chart of the story's data; never restate post text as media. 2) Text: it opens on a bare result ('A contract risk model reached 86.20% accuracy...') with no setting. Say first what the project is and what problem it solves, for whom, then the result. 3) It ends on a question; end with one plain sentence on what the work now lets someone do.

rules: unsupported by the facts: Claim that predicting cancellations 'improved' with a new model (FACTS describe building a new model, not improving an existing one).

unsupported by the facts: Causal link between the model's good ROC-AUC and the decision to deploy it (FACTS state both the ROC-AUC and the deployment decision, but do not explicitly state that the ROC-AUC was the reason for the deployment).
unsupported by the facts: Claim that reliably detecting sensor spikes and preventing device failures without false alarms was 'the engineering challenge'.
